### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/verify`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/architecture.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext), getServices (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via getDriverByName (symbol, a field of interface GuardedEngine))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext))_
- `content/docs/plugins/anatomy.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext), getServices (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext))_
- `content/docs/plugins/development.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a method of interface ManagedDriverGuardContext))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **8** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f86104ed55c7799c4f8315b227475289bcecc15c` — the merge of head `26abb3e92ac6425918f7300086f126544594c421` into base `1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f86104ed55c7799c4f8315b227475289bcecc15c && git checkout f86104ed55c7799c4f8315b227475289bcecc15c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b 26abb3e92ac6425918f7300086f126544594c421 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b && git merge --no-ff 26abb3e92ac6425918f7300086f126544594c421

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 6c1965975d6a908872465ef704e2a7dfe1e05b34

- **Shape:** `l1-face.mjs --pr 36171` at 6c1965975d: open, draft, base main; first line `Fixes #35640`, which delivers the ruling's single PR (ruling item 4); no closing keyword on any other card; the changeset covers `@objectstack/verify`, the one published package touched; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` · `Metadata-protocol: none`; `Skills-docs: none …` is true (no `skills/**` teaches verify's stand-in rule, and the verify README is updated).
  - Its one flag, dogfood owed for `!` plus the narrowing arm, is met. The dev report 7066896452 records `dogfood_battery` = "6c1965975 · os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 … Test Files 483 passed | 3 skipped (486) · Tests 4101 passed | 68 skipped (4169) · no failures": the full battery, pinned to this head.
- **The ruling (7065449898), item by item, checked in the diff:**
  1. **Every shipped engine is stood in, `mongodb` included.** `managedStandInEngine` now returns `memory` for `memory` and the default store's engine for every other id `resolveDriverId` knows. That is the spec's driver vocabulary, the same table the default factory's `supports()` reads. It replaces the old `SQL_ENGINES` set that left `mongodb` out.
     - The federation-only ids (`oracle`, `mssql`) and the retired `mongo` are refused managed at parse in `datasource.zod.ts`, so the wider table admits no pairing a real boot would take.
     - derive's "managed, no stand-in" withheld branch and its sentence are removed, and `hasManagedStandIn` goes. It was not exported from the package root, so no public API changed.
  2. **A plugin driver id refuses the boot.** `bootClaimed` calls `unstandableManagedDatasources(config)` and throws before composing. The check reads the same `isManagedDatasource` as the factory and derive, skips `default`, and handles both the array and the name-keyed map.
     - The sentence names each datasource and its driver id (`JSON.stringify`) and says why. The dev measured `os verify` on the built CLI exiting 1 with it.
     - The verify factory also refuses rather than handing such a managed spec to the real factory. External specs still go to `opts.real.create` unchanged.
  3. **No switch:** the diff adds no CLI flag, boot option, metadata key or exported member. Only three `src` files change, plus text.
  4. **One PR.**
- **Premise P2 was checked first:** the dev's read in 7066896452 names the plugin's own registration, ObjectQL's adoption of the driver and the already-registered branch. It agrees with the ruling's P2. I did not re-read those files: the ruling marks P2 as read, not measured, and the refusal pin is the behavioural proof.
- **Pins and controls** (`verify.managed-datasource-stand-in.test.ts`, 23 tests):
  - A mongodb datasource behind a TCP listener that counts connections: 0 connections, CRUD verified, seed and hook rows read back in memory. CONTROL: the factory `os dev` uses does connect.
  - A plugin driver id: boot rejected with the datasource and driver named, and the recording driver never called. CONTROL: the same plugin behind an EXTERNAL datasource initialises and serves a REST create, so external is unchanged.
  - The dev reported four reverse legs: base source 8 ✗, mongodb mapped to undefined 3 ✗, the refusal line deleted 1 ✗, a mongodb withhold re-added in derive 1 ✗, each restored to the HEAD blob. I did not re-run them.
- **Changeset and docs, read sentence by sentence:**
  - The changeset's two bullets, the FROM/TO/fix lines and the "external … not affected" line match the diff.
  - Its `adr-0087: not-required` reason holds: no key, value or export moves.
  - The supersede sentence is the right route for the two unreleased changesets on main, which this PR may not edit.
  - The `cli.mdx` `os verify` paragraph and the README Posture paragraph say the same as the `harness.ts` and stand-in headers.
- **Gates:** 40 success, 15 expected skip, 0 unexpected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending at 6c1965975d. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are both success. The local NOT MEASURED families (`check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3, two repo-wide scans timed out at 300 s) are covered by green CI.
- **Accepted, recorded:**
  - The `os validate` observation: author-time rules pass a managed plugin-driver datasource. No defect class is claimed, so it is not filed.
  - The verify report does not say an object ran on a stand-in, which the ruling leaves out of scope.
- **Landing:** `!` plus `(narrowing)`, so a contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed on this head. The area runs it, and then the PR goes to the seat for approvers (Tier H); the area does not land it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6c1965975d6a908872465ef704e2a7dfe1e05b34`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/verify/src/managed-datasource-stand-in.ts, packages/verify/src/harness.ts, packages/verify/src/derive.ts, packages/verify/src/derive.test.ts, packages/verify/src/verify.managed-datasource-stand-in.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/data/driver/config-registry.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-connection-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/default-datasource-driver-factory.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/driver-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/plugin.ts, packages/verify/src/artifact-collections.ts, packages/verify/src/index.ts, docs/adr/0062-external-datasource-runtime.md, content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx

PR #36171, card #35640, ruling 7065449898 (C+A). Inputs: the card body and its 10 comments, the PR body and file list (8 files), the net diff against merge base `411fe24b4394`, the tree at the head, and the 55 check-runs on the head. PR comments were not read.

Gate verdicts (check-runs on the head): 55 runs, 40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. Success includes Test Core and its 10 shards, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates and every lint lane, Build Core, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards. Skipped are the UI lanes, the opt-in lanes, Temporal Conformance, the queue-verdict lanes and `Dogfood Verify CLI` (run 136927714278); none of them is a failure, and none was re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

- `managedStandInEngine` accept-set: every id `resolveDriverId` answers now gets a stand-in (`memory` → memory, every other one → the default store's engine). That adds `mongodb`, the federation-only `oracle` and `mssql`, and every alias face of the table. **Right**: it is ruling item 1, and `resolveDriverId` is the same reader the default factory's `supports()` uses (`default-datasource-driver-factory.ts`, `resolveKind`), so "shipped" has one definition.
- `unstandableManagedDatasources` refuse-set: a declared datasource, not named `default`, that `isManagedDatasource` reads as managed (declared or defaulted) and whose driver id does not resolve. Reads the top level, else `packages[]`, and a name-keyed map. **Right** against ruling item 2 as written. It is keyed on the driver id; see S1 for what that key does not cover.
- `bootClaimed`: the refusal is the first statement, before `NODE_ENV` is set and before the kernel exists; `bootStack`'s catch releases the configuration claim. `bootClaimed` is the only place this package builds a kernel, and `bootStackOnce` goes through `bootStack`. **Right**.
- `createVerifyDatasourceDriverFactory.create`: a managed spec on an unshipped id now throws instead of reaching the real factory. **Right** (fail, not fall back). Not reachable from the connection service, whose `supports()` gate comes first.
- `deriveCrudCases`: the "managed, no stand-in" withheld branch is gone, so objects on managed `mongodb` and on managed plugin-driver datasources are derived. **Right** for `mongodb`. For a plugin driver id it is right only behind the boot refusal: `deriveCrudCases` is a public export (`index.ts`), and called on its own it no longer withholds those objects. No caller in the tree does that.
- Public surface: `hasManagedStandIn` is removed and three functions are added, all in a module `index.ts` does not re-export. No published export moves. **Right**.
- No spec schema, no metadata key, no CLI flag, no boot option changes. **Right** (ruling item 3).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/35640-verify-memory-stand-in.md`: `@objectstack/verify` patch, title with `!`, a BREAKING entry with FROM, TO and the fix, one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), both declaration lines. Check Changeset is success on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — matches. Nothing a metadata author can write is added, removed or refused by the spec, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner (AGENTS.md, changeset rule). The narrowing arm is right: a boot that ran now refuses. The PR body and the changeset carry the same two lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report (7066896452). Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag 1, two unreleased changesets on `main` still say `mongodb` and plugin drivers keep their real driver: answered as N3 below. Prose, not a blocker.
- Dev flag 2, `os validate` passes a managed datasource on an unshipped driver id: answered as N2 below. Confirmed in `datasource.zod.ts`: the spec refuses `managed` only for a federation-only driver and for `external.connector`; an unknown id on `managed` parses.
- Ruling premise P2: read and it holds. The connection service returns `already-registered` when the engine already holds a driver under the datasource's name, before it looks at the factory; `ObjectQLPlugin` adopts every `driver.*` service. The premise is what S1 is built on.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: the spec does **not** refuse a managed datasource on a plugin's driver id. `driver` is an open namespace (`config-registry.zod.ts`, "Where the boundary is"), and the runtime delivers such a datasource under `os dev` and `os serve` through the plugin's own driver. So this is not the spec's own refusal made real. It is also not a declared capability taken away at a consumer in the sense the rule forbids: the capability stays whole in the runtime, and what is refused is running `os verify` over it, because verify cannot keep its "writes only to stores it creates" rule there. The maintainer ruled exactly this refusal, with no switch, and declined the two ways of delivering instead (a mongodb-compatible store, a plugin contract for an ephemeral store). The narrowing is the ruled one, and the mongodb half removes a withheld state rather than adding one. I accept the design on that basis.

Tried to break it:

- S1 (should-fix) — The refusal is keyed on the declared driver id, and the bypass it guards against is keyed on the datasource name. `attemptConnect` (`datasource-connection-service.ts`, the `engine.getDriverByName(name)` guard) answers `already-registered` for any datasource whose name a driver is already registered under, and never reads `record.driver` on that path. A plugin in the app's `plugins` that registers `driver.NAME` (the shape `packages/runtime/src/driver-plugin.ts` and `driver-odata` use, and the shape this PR's own recording plugin uses) for a managed datasource that declares a **shipped** id, for example `{ name: 'docs', driver: 'mongodb' }`, is therefore neither refused nor stood in: `unstandableManagedDatasources` passes it because `mongodb` resolves, verify's factory is never asked, and the plugin's real driver takes the seed, the hooks and the flows. With this PR derive no longer withholds a `mongodb` object, so verify's own CRUD, delete-behaviour and unique-scope writes go there too, where before they were withheld. The SQL ids have had the same gap since PR #35635; this PR extends it to `mongodb` and at the same time states the rule without exception ("never connected to the database it names, on any engine the platform ships", README, both headers, `cli.mdx`, the changeset). Reach is narrow: it needs a driver registered under the datasource's own name, and the shipped drivers carry fixed names, so it takes a custom or renamed driver. The `onEnable` escape hatch does not open it, since `connectDeclared` runs before `onEnable` and the first registration wins. Nothing in the test file pins this case; the refusal pin and its control both use an unshipped id. Fix, either: refuse (or fail the boot) when a declared managed datasource other than `default` ends up on a driver verify's factory did not build, so the check follows the mechanism P2 describes; or have the seat record on the card that this case is accepted, and bound the sentences that say "never". The first moves the head and needs a delta review.
- N1 (nit) — `unstandableManagedDatasourceRefusal` states as fact that the datasource is "supplied by a plugin". An unresolvable id can also be a misspelt shipped id (`postgress`), and a datasource with no `driver` prints `driver undefined`. The boot is rightly refused in both cases; only the stated cause is a guess. Wording, in a code file, so a fix moves the head: leave as an accepted deviation or fold into the S1 delta.
- N2 (nit) — The first place an author learns that a managed plugin-driver datasource cannot be verified is `os verify` itself; `os validate` passes it and the spec says nothing. The ruling forbids a new key or flag and expects no spec change, so this is not this PR's to fix. A follow-up card for triage, if the seat wants the author told earlier.
- N3 (nit) — `.changeset/verify-managed-datasource-stand-in.md` and `.changeset/35640-verify-real-store-wording.md` on `main` will ship in the same release notes and say the opposite of this one. The new changeset says it supersedes them, which is enough to read correctly. Editing or dropping the two older sentences is a prose-face change for whoever compiles the release.

Checked and found sound: the refusal precedes every side effect and releases the claim; `default` is excluded consistently in the refusal and in derive; external and validate-only datasources are untouched, as ruled on #35255; the refusal fires for a managed plugin-driver datasource even when no object binds it, which is the ruling's "while one is declared"; the test file's mongodb pin has a real control (the default factory connects to the same listener), and the refusal pin asserts the plugin never initialised.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), three nits (N1, N2, N3).

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (delta) · head a81e77767266735a04481fffb7c7d26bb050abf8

Delta read only: `6c1965975d..a81e777672`, 6 files, +195/−27. It answers contract review 7067086844 (S1 and N1). The ACCEPT 7067006119 on 6c1965975d stands for everything outside this delta.

- **Shape:** `l1-face.mjs --pr 36171` at a81e777672 is clean except its dogfood flag. The flag is met: report 7067886738 gives `dogfood_battery` = "a81e77767 · os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · Tests 4101 passed | 68 skipped (4169) · no failures", the full battery on this head. The first line, declarations, changeset coverage and `Skills-docs:` are unchanged and still true.
- **S1, checked in the diff:** `createManagedDatasourceDriverGuard` refuses when a `driver.NAME` service or an engine driver (`getDriverByName`) is held under the name of any managed datasource other than `default`, whatever driver id the datasource declares. `bootClaimed` mounts it with `kernel.use` before `ObjectQLPlugin`, and nothing is mounted on that kernel before it.
  - **Why its `start()` comes before any write:**
    - `resolvePluginOrder` (`packages/core/src/plugin-order.ts`) keeps insertion order for plugins with no edges, and the guard declares no dependencies, so it is first in the ordered list.
    - The kernel runs Phase 1 (init) for every plugin before Phase 2 (start) for any plugin (`kernel.ts`), so the guard's `start()` sees every init-time `driver.*` registration and runs before ObjectQL adopts drivers or AppPlugin connects and seeds.
    - The pre-compose refusal for an unshipped driver id stays in place (`harness.ts:1003`).
  - No key, flag, boot option or package export is added. The guard is a module-level export of `src`, not of the package root.
- **Pin and control:**
  - The new pin uses a recording plugin that registers `driver.vmd_docs_ds` under a managed datasource declaring `mongodb`, with a seed. The boot rejects with a message naming `datasource "vmd_docs_ds" (driver "mongodb")` and "registered a driver of its own". The recorded calls are exactly `[plugin.init]`: no connect, no schema sync and no seed write.
  - The control is the existing boot, where the same plugin sits behind an EXTERNAL datasource. It initialises and takes the REST create, still green, so the guard does not catch external datasources. The managed `mongodb` stand-in boot in the same suite also still passes, so the guard does not fire on the platform's own registrations.
  - Ablation, from the dev's reading (I did not re-run it): with the `throw` line deleted, the boot succeeds on the plugin's driver and the run is `Tests 1 failed | 24 passed (25)`. The file was restored to the HEAD blob.
  - The boot refusal is a thrown boot error, not an ADR-0112 HTTP envelope, so a message assert is the right pin, as in round 0.
- **N1:** the refusal now reads "names no driver id the platform ships (a plugin's driver, or a misspelling)", and a missing driver prints `(no driver declared)`. A unit pin covers the second.
- **Text, read sentence by sentence:**
  - The changeset's second BREAKING bullet (FROM/TO/fix) matches the guard. The "external … not affected" line moved under it and is still true.
  - The `cli.mdx` `os verify` paragraph and the README Posture paragraph say the same as the guard: it refuses before any plugin starts, whatever driver id is declared, and there is no switch.
  - The PR body has been brought to this head: a round-1 bullet, the third pin, the ablation reading and the report pointer.
- **Gates:** 42 success, 17 expected skip, 0 unexpected skip, 0 failed and 0 pending at a81e777672. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are both success. The 3 local NOT MEASURED families are covered by green CI.
- **Recorded, unchanged from round 0:** the report's two "noted, not filed" items:
  - `os validate` passing an unshipped managed driver id was accepted in round 0, since no defect class is claimed.
  - The two older unreleased changesets are superseded by this one's last paragraph.
  - Neither one is a residual this PR leaves open.
- **Landing:** unchanged. `!` plus `(narrowing)` makes this Tier H. The Fable delta contract review on this head is owed by the area, and then the PR goes to the seat. The area does not land it.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed. For the shape it named (a plugin registering `driver.NAME` in `init()`, as `DriverPlugin` and `driver-odata` do) the boot is refused before any plugin starts, and the new pin shows the plugin's driver recording `plugin.init` and nothing else. The dev's ablation of the throw turns that pin red.

N1: closed. The sentence no longer asserts a plugin as the cause, and a missing driver is printed as `(no driver declared)`, pinned.

Tried to break the guard:

- S2 (should-fix) — The guard does not cover every way a driver comes to hold a managed datasource's name before verify's stand-in does, and its jsdoc says it does.
  - Key mismatch. The guard looks up the service key `driver.NAME`. `ObjectQLPlugin.start` adopts every `driver.*` service with `registerDriver(service)`, and the engine keys the driver on the instance's own `name` (`engine-registration.ts`), not on the service key. A plugin that registers `driver.anything` holding a driver whose `name` is the managed datasource's name passes both guard checks (no such service key; the engine holds nothing yet), is adopted under the datasource's name one start later, and the connection service then answers `already-registered`. The jsdoc sentence "at the first `start()` every such registration is visible" is not true for it.
  - Window after the guard. The stand-in is registered at `AppPlugin.start` (or in AppPlugin's own `objectql:drivers-ready` handler, for mapping-routed datasources only), not at the guard's start. Between the two, `ObjectQLPlugin.start` fires the exported `objectql:drivers-ready` hook with the engine. A plugin that subscribes in `init()` and calls `engine.registerDriver` there takes the name of an object-bound managed datasource first. The jsdoc sentence "A driver registered later cannot take the name: the connection service has registered verify's stand-in by then" is false for that window; it holds only after `AppPlugin.start`.
  - Both need a hand-written plugin, so reach is narrower than S1's was; neither shipped driver shape does this. Read from the code, not measured.
  - Fix, either: compare each `driver.*` service's own `name` (not only its key) against the managed names, and re-check the engine for those names where the stand-in is about to be built or at `objectql:drivers-ready`; or correct the two jsdoc sentences to what the guard covers and have the seat accept the rest on the card. The first moves the head and needs a delta review. The prose faces (README, `cli.mdx`, changeset) describe the refusal, not completeness, and need no change for the second route.
- N4 (nit) — The guard's refusal reaches the caller wrapped by the kernel: `Plugin com.objectstack.verify.managed-datasource-driver-guard failed to start - rollback complete: verify: refusing to boot: …`, and the kernel also prints the stack to stderr. The driver-id refusal is thrown bare. The sentence is intact and the pin asserts on its content, so this is presentation only.
- N5 (nit) — The guard is an ordinary named plugin, and `kernel.use` lets a later plugin with the same `name` supersede an earlier one. An app plugin that takes the guard's name removes it. That is deliberate sabotage of one's own verify run, not an accident an author can fall into; noted, no action asked.

Checked and found sound: a plugin that registers in `start()` is too late to be adopted as a `driver.*` service (adoption runs once, in `ObjectQLPlugin.start`), and app plugins start after `AppPlugin`, where `registerDriver` keeps the stand-in already registered; a driver put on the engine directly in `init()` is caught by the `getDriverByName` leg; `default` and external datasources are left alone; a managed datasource nothing routes to is refused too when a plugin holds its name, which matches the ruling's "while one is declared"; the guard degrades to the service-key check, not to silence, when the `objectql` service is absent. One limit carried from round 0, outside this delta: both refusals and the guard read the datasources of the configuration handed to `bootStack`, not ones a plugin entry might declare on its own.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S2), two nits (N4, N5). S1: closed. N1: closed. N2, N3: untouched by the delta.
